label: Transformed Schopenhauer's passive Will to Live into active, life-affirming Will to Power
description: The young Nietzsche was profoundly shaken by Schopenhauer's unflinching metaphysical pessimism. In his mature philosophy, Nietzsche inverted Schopenhauer's ascetical denial of the Will into life-affirming Dionysian intoxication and the Will to Power (Wille zur Macht).
dialecticalTension: Pessimistic Buddhist-style denial of the will (asceticism and resignation) versus Radical tragic affirmation of life and the Will to Power.
historicalContext: Leipzig and Basel, 1865–1886. Nietzsche discovered Schopenhauer's book in a second-hand bookstore in 1865, calling him his 'educator', before breaking with him in Untimely Meditations and Genealogy of Morality.

citations.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
citations.quote: The world viewed from inside, the world defined and determined according to its 'intelligible character' — it would be 'will to power' and nothing else.

citations.author: R. Lanier Anderson
citations.sectionOrPage: Section 4. The Will to Power and Critique of Morals

label: Formulated and introduced The World as Will & Metaphysical Pessimism
description: Arthur Schopenhauer formulated and introduced the concept of "The World as Will & Metaphysical Pessimism", which became a seminal contribution in metaphysics philosophy.
dialecticalTension: Formulating an epistemic apparatus to resolve central problems in metaphysics.
historicalContext: Introduced during the 19th Century Divergences as part of Arthur Schopenhauer's canonical writings.
